_comment: Copy to council-agents.json (gitignored) and keep only the agents you actually run. The launcher takes the command ONLY from this file, never from the council record, so convening a council can never choose what executes on your machine.

claude-code._doc: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless - -p runs the full agent loop non-interactively. --mcp-config is passed a file the launcher writes OUTSIDE the worktree, because it holds a bearer token. Do NOT add --bare: it skips MCP discovery.

codex._doc: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/24135 - codex exec AUTO-CANCELS MCP tool calls non-interactively. The council is entirely MCP tool calls, so with these args codex will join and then stall. The only known workaround today is to add "--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox", which disables the sandbox: uncomment it only if you accept that on this machine. MCP server must already be in ~/.codex/config.toml.
codex.warn: codex exec cancels MCP tool calls unless you add --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox (openai/codex#24135) - it will likely stall after joining

cursor._doc: https://cursor.com/docs/cli/headless - --force pre-approves edits in print mode. MCP server must already be in ~/.cursor/mcp.json. Known upstream bug: -p can hang without releasing the terminal on some early-2026 builds.

antigravity._doc: https://antigravity.google/docs/cli/headless - --print-timeout defaults to 5m, far below a 90m council, so it is raised here. Shell commands are soft-denied in headless mode unless allowed: add permissions.allow rules in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json (preferred) or append --dangerously-skip-permissions.
